Base oil guide

Re-refined base oil: the questions that protect a blend.

RRBO can be used in suitable lubricant, grease and industrial fluid formulations. The important decision is the verified grade and repeatability of the supplier's batches.

View base oil ↗ Call sales

The Indian standard covers virgin Group I to Group III base oils and re-refined Group I base oils. A marketing label should never replace the latest laboratory report.

Start with the applicable standard

IS 18722 (Part 1):2024 defines requirements and test methods for mineral-origin base oils. It states that the re-refined base oils covered by the standard pertain to Group I.

Review the properties that matter

  • Kinematic viscosity and viscosity index.
  • Sulphur and saturates.
  • Flash point, colour and visible impurities.
  • Variation across more than one batch.

Be careful with Group II claims

The standard defines Group II using at least 90% saturates and no more than 0.03% sulphur. Ask for a report that proves both before accepting the label or price.

Five supplier questions

  1. Which grade is this and can I see the current COA?
  2. How do key results vary across batches?
  3. Where and how is the oil re-refined?
  4. What documentation accompanies the order?
  5. Can I validate a sample in my own blend?

Reference: BIS publication bulletin listing IS 18722 (Part 1):2024. Ask BIS for the current complete standard before making a conformity claim.
